headline: Himachal: Russian paraglider gets stuck in high-tension electricity wires; rescued
content: Shimla, Nov 10 (PTI) A Russian paraglider in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi, who got entangled in high-tension electricity wires over 100 metres above the ground, was rescued after a 3-hour-long operation on Tuesday, police said. The incident occurred today near Tandu, when Alexey (48) took off from Bir Billing and got stuck in the wires mid-flight. Following the incident, he immediately sent pictures of his location to the Bir Billing Paragliding Association to seek help. The association then alerted the district administration and dispatched rescue teams to the location. The rescue operation was jointly carried out by the teams of the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Gawar Company. Considering the potential danger of falling, the teams also laid nets and mattresses on the road. Machinery, including a crane, was used to rescue the pilot. He was safely rescued following a three-hour-long rescue operation. He was taken to the Zonal hospital in Mandi, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Chander Prakash said. PTI COR BPL APL

headline: Paraglider stranded on high-tension wires 150 metres above ground for 2.5 hours in Himachal Pradesh
content: SHIMLA: A paraglider was rescued after remaining suspended from high-tension power lines at a height of around 150 metres for nearly two-and-a-half hours in Himachal Pradesh's Mandi district on Tuesday.The administration used a 146-metre hydraulic crane to bring him to safety in a challenging rescue operation near Mehar village, around five kilometres from Mandi town.The pilot got entangled in the power lines along the Pathankot-Mandi highway in the afternoon. Other paragliders immediately alerted the administration, following which the power supply was switched off, an official said.Mandi SDM and police officials rushed to the spot, but rescuing the pilot from such a height posed a major challenge. The administration immediately arranged a 146-metre crane for the operation.An SDRF personnel used the crane's basket to reach the stranded paraglider and managed to bring him down safely.As a precautionary measure, people gathered at the spot spread a tarpaulin and mattresses on the ground beneath the stranded pilot in case he fell during the operation.The Pathankot-Mandi highway was closed to heavy vehicles while the crane was being assembled and the rescue operation was underway.Stay updated with the latest Shimla news. headline: Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College who empowered rural women, dies at 81
content: Sanjit Bunker Roy, the social activist who gave rural communities, particularly women, the skills and confidence to transform their villages without depending on formal education or conventional institutions, died on Tuesday at the age of 81.Roy, the founder of Barefoot College in Tilonia, Rajasthan, dedicated more than five decades to rural development and empowering marginalised communities. His funeral was held in Tilonia, where he had established the institution and made his home."Bunker Roy passed away peacefully at 6.15 am with Aruna Roy (wife) and others by his side. He went as he wanted to, in his own home in Tilonia, surrounded by some of the countless people who loved and cared for him deeply and passionately," the statement released by people close to him said.Like Mahatma Gandhi’s visit to Bihar in 1917 marked a foundational chapter in India’s freedom struggle, Roy’s life also changed after a visit to Palamu (now in Jharkhand) in 1965 famine acquainted him with poverty and hunger.Speaking at Ted Talks in 2011, Roy said, “The whole world was laid out for me. Everything was at my feet. Then I thought out of curiosity to see what a village looks like. In 1965 I went to what is called the worst Bihar famine and I saw starvation, death and hunger for the first time.”Author Amitav Ghosh recalled that Roy was a champion squash player and could have been a top diplomat, bureaucrat or corporate honcho but instead he chose to dedicate his life to alleviating poverty in rural India. “He was a true hero,” he said.Barefoot College trains marginalised illiterate and semi-literate women from the Global South to become Solar Engineers. They learn how to design, make, install and repair solar lanterns and home-lighting systems and have become affectionately known as “Solar Mamas”. The organisation follows a Gandhian philosophy that believes technology should be demystified and there is a difference between literacy and education.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said, “By founding the Barefoot College in Tilonia, Rajasthan, he transcended conventional notions of formal education, proving that illiterate and semi-literate villagers, especially women, possessed the wisdom, skill and capability to build, innovate and lead. His extraordinary vision of training rural grandmothers into "Barefoot Solar Engineers" illuminated thousands of off-grid homes across India and the developing world, leaving behind an indelible legacy of dignity, community empowerment, and environmental stewardship,” he said.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh recalled Roy playing a key role in creating vast new opportunities for what were then called 'voluntary agencies' in development schemes and programmes.“This was at the personal initiative of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Bunker Roy became a close associate of Sam Pitroda also in the implementation of the various Technology Missions especially in drinking water, immunisation and adult literacy. In later years, he would smilingly say that he was recognised as being the husband of the legendary Aruna Roy, who had resigned from the IAS in the mid-1970s to join him in Tilonia. Her 2024 memoir, The Personal is Political, is a wonderful account of their journey together,” Ramesh said.

headline: SC orders SIT probe into illegal gravel mining in Rajasthan’s Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers
content: The Supreme Court has ordered a probe by a Special Investigation Team (SIT) into illegal bajri (gravel) mining in Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries in Rajasthan.While directing the Rajasthan Government to set up an SIT to investigate illegal mining, a Bench led by Justice Vikram Nath also ordered a probe into the alleged involvement of public officials in facilitating such illegal activities.The SIT will examine if public officials facilitated or enabled illegal mining, including instances of collusion, dereliction of duty or failure to act despite knowledge of violations. Appropriate action has to be initiated against those found responsible.The Bench — which also included Justice Sandeep Mehta — directed the SIT to file a status report before it on or before the next date of hearing on November 27.It restrained the state government from granting permissions for the establishment of new industrial units along or in the vicinity of the riverine ecosystem until the High Flood Line and buffer zones are scientifically determined.It said the SIT shall be headed by an officer not below the rank of Inspector General of Police and will include the Superintendents of Police of Jodhpur, Balotra and Pali.“The SIT shall undertake a comprehensive investigation into organised illegal bajri mining activities affecting the Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries. The investigation shall extend to identifying the persons and entities involved in such activities, the networks through which the illegal extraction, transportation and sale of bajri are organised, and the beneficiaries of such operations,” it said in its October 26 order.The order came during the hearing of a suo motu case on pollution in the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, affecting the environment and the lives of approximately 20 lakh people.Earlier, the Bench had warned Rajasthan authorities of a CBI probe into alleged illegal mining and the regularisation of mining areas along the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system. It had sought to know why the state authorities granted mining leases in areas where illegal mining had been detected, and regularising illegal leases.It ordered that an additional protective zone of 100 metres be maintained on either side of the respective recorded outer boundaries of the rivers. The Court held that No Red Category industry shall be permitted to be established within a distance of 500 metres from the said recorded outer boundaries.The Bench expressed serious concern over the Rajasthan Mining Department's explanation that mining leases had been subsequently granted according to prescribed procedures in several areas where illegal gravel mining had previously been detected.“The fact that mining leases may have subsequently been granted in accordance with the prescribed procedure does not, by itself, answer the question whether the grant of such leases is environmentally sustainable or consistent with the need to preserve and restore the natural course, riverbed and ecological integrity of the river systems,” it said, adding the authorities attempted to legitimise illegal mining activities through subsequent lease grants instead of taking appropriate action against those responsible.The Bench said it would consider directing appropriate action against officers found responsible for permitting or facilitating such activities.“We deprecate the apparent attempt on the part of the Mining Department of the State of Rajasthan to legitimise illegal mining activities being carried out in the riverbeds by subsequently granting mining leases, rather than taking appropriate action against those responsible. We shall consider directing appropriate action against the officers found responsible for permitting or facilitating such activities,” it said.

headline: NIT Raipur Lays Foundation Stone for ₹88.76-Crore Centre of Excellence to Boost Innovation and Entrepreneurship
content: National Institute of Technology Raipur on Tuesday laid the foundation stone for the ₹88.76-crore Smt. Mithilesh Agrawal Centre of Excellence for Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Engineering and Technology (MACIEET), marking a significant step towards strengthening Chhattisgarh's innovation, research and startup ecosystem. The centre is being established through a joint initiative of the Motilal Oswal Foundation, the Government of Chhattisgarh and NIT Raipur, with funding shared in the ratio of 80:10:10. The Motilal Oswal Foundation will contribute ₹71.008 crore, while the State Government and NIT Raipur will contribute ₹8.876 crore each. The project will be implemented through the NIT Raipur Foundation for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (NITRRFIE), a Section 8 company of the institute. Named after Smt. Mithilesh Agrawal, mother of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited Chairman and Co-founder Shri Raamdeo Agrawal, the centre is envisioned as a comprehensive hub for advanced technology, skill development, research, incubation and entrepreneurship. Shri Raamdeo Agrawal hails from Nagpura village near Raipur. The foundation stone ceremony was attended by Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, Shri Raamdeo Agrawal, Chairman and Co-founder of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited, Dr. Suresh Haware, Chairman of the Board of Governors of NIT Raipur, and Dr. N. V. Ramana Rao, Director of NIT Raipur. Registrar Ashok K. Gupta, Dr. Sameer Bajpai, Head of the Career Development Centre, Dr. Anuj K. Shukla, Faculty-in-Charge of NITRRFIE, Dhamtari District Magistrate Shri Avinash Mishra, and other faculty members, officials, alumni, students and distinguished guests were also present. Designed by INI Design Studio around the concept of a 'Learning Street', the centre will be a ground-plus-six-storey building spread across a built-up area of approximately 12,307 square metres. The L-shaped structure will feature a landscaped courtyard, an open-air amphitheatre, a double-skin façade for climate control and rooftop solar panels. The design also incorporates existing trees on the site, with a focus on sustainability and an environment-friendly campus. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai said MACIEET would provide the youth of Chhattisgarh with access to world-class laboratories, mentoring and incubation facilities within the State. He said the State Government was proud to be associated with the initiative, which would help transform young people's ideas into enterprises and employment opportunities, while advancing the vision of Viksit Chhattisgarh and Viksit Bharat.

headline: Himachal: Baddi Police form special teams to nab accused in Nalagarh firing incident; one injured
content: Nalagarh (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 10 (ANI): The Baddi Police have constituted special teams to arrest a man accused of opening fire on another person near the Lakad Depot on Ramshahar Road in Nalagarh on Tuesday.The victim, identified as Mohammad Aslam alias Ballu, sustained gunshot injuries in the incident.According to the police, the incident took place within the jurisdiction of Nalagarh Police Station. Aslam, son of Ghulam Rasool and a resident of Ward No. 7, Nalagarh, was rushed to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Nalagarh, for medical treatment.On the basis of a complaint lodged by Joginder Singh, son of Santokh Singh, a resident of village Pannar in Nalagarh tehsil, police registered a case under Sections 109 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 25, 54 and 59 of the Arms Act.As per the complaint, the accused, identified as Sahil, son of Rajender Singh and a resident of Nalagarh, allegedly fired multiple shots at Aslam before fleeing the spot on a motorcycle.Taking serious note of the incident, Baddi Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar (Vinod Dhiman, as mentioned in the press release) visited the crime scene and reviewed the situation. He also directed police officials to take immediate steps to apprehend the accused.Superintendent of Police Baddi Vinod Kumar said that "We have constituted multiple special police teams to ensure the early arrest of the accused. The teams are investigating all aspects of the incident and conducting searches at possible hideouts. Efforts are underway to apprehend the accused at the earliest."Police said that the investigation into the case was in progress and teams were pursuing various leads to trace and arrest the accused. (ANI)

headline: Sukhu Launches 26 Projects Worth Rs. 1.75 bn in Chamba
content: Sukhu formed a committee to discuss with the Centre the demand for Scheduled Tribe status for 27 gram panchayats in the constituency. He announced that the state government would soon introduce the Mukhya Mantri Ka Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojana, which will cover more than 300,000 families with annual incomes below Rs. 75,000. Under the proposed scheme, eligible women aged 21 to 59 will receive monthly assistance of Rs. 1,500. The package will also provide 300 units of free electricity and health insurance coverage of Rs. 1 mn, according to officials. The chief minister announced Rs. 180 mn for construction of the Holi-Utrala road and said CBSE-affiliated schools would open at Lylh, Mehla, Bharmour, Sunara and Holi from the next academic session. The government will also examine proposals to upgrade schools at Churi, Chadi, Ananaihar, Grundhi and Kunaid, and assess a suitable location for a helipad. headline: Burning Fields, Choking Cities: North India’s Air Pollution Crisis Crosses Borders
content: New Delhi/Shimla: The arrival of November has once again brought a familiar but alarming environmental crisis to northern India. Thick layers of smog have enveloped Delhi and several cities in Punjab and Haryana, while Lahore and other parts of Pakistan’s Punjab province are also struggling with deteriorating air quality. Adding to the regional concern, industrial towns in Himachal Pradesh, particularly Baddi, are witnessing a worrying rise in pollution levels, challenging the perception that the hill state is relatively insulated from the air-quality crisis affecting the northern plains. The crisis is being driven by multiple factors, including agricultural residue burning, Diwali firecracker emissions, vehicular exhaust, industrial pollution, construction dust and unfavourable meteorological conditions. The combined effect has pushed several urban and industrial centres into unhealthy air-quality categories. What makes the situation particularly concerning is that pollution is no longer an isolated problem affecting Delhi or a few industrial cities. It has become a regional environmental challenge involving the entire northwestern plains and neighbouring areas across the international border. For millions of residents, the consequences are increasingly visible in everyday life: hazy skies, reduced visibility, irritation in the eyes and throat, breathing difficulties and growing concerns over long-term health consequences. The national capital has once again emerged as the centre of the regional air pollution crisis. Following Diwali celebrations, Delhi witnessed a sharp deterioration in air quality, with the CPCB recording an average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 376 on November 9, placing it in the ‘very poor’ category. Several areas experienced even worse conditions, with independent monitoring platforms reporting exceptionally high readings. The combination of firecracker emissions, agricultural smoke, vehicular pollution and industrial activities contributed to the deterioration.

headline: Himachal Pradesh: Paraglider Pilot Rescued After Getting Tangled in High-Tension Wires in Mandi
content: A paraglider pilot was successfully rescued in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district after becoming entangled in high-tension electricity wires approximately 150 feet above the ground. An Air Force helicopter, which had been requisitioned as a precautionary measure, was ultimately stood down following the success of the ground rescue operation. Information was available with The Chenab Times that the incident occurred in Mehar village, situated about five kilometres from Mandi city along the Pathankot-Mandi national highway. The pilot found himself ensnared in the live wires, leaving him suspended at a considerable altitude over the road. Local residents promptly alerted the authorities and ensured the electricity supply to the affected wires was cut off. Officials acknowledged that conducting a rescue at such a height presented significant challenges. Following the notification, administrative officials, including the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) of Mandi and police officers, quickly arrived at the scene. In a bid to enhance safety, local villagers also unfurled a tarpaulin on the ground beneath the stranded pilot, providing a potential cushion in the event of a fall. Mandi Deputy Commissioner Apoorv Devgan confirmed that the administration had received intelligence regarding the paraglider’s predicament. He stated that a dedicated team was actively engaged in the rescue efforts. In an update provided during the operation, Mr. Devgan indicated that a crane had been brought to the location and expressed hope that it would facilitate the pilot’s extraction. He also noted the requisition of an Air Force helicopter, which was prepared to deploy if the ground operation proved unsuccessful. Ultimately, ground teams from the district administration, utilizing the crane, managed to extricate the pilot from his precarious position. The Air Force helicopter’s intervention was rendered unnecessary, and it was subsequently dismissed after the successful conclusion of the rescue mission. The pilot’s condition following the rescue was not immediately detailed. The incident highlights the inherent risks associated with adventure sports, even when conducted in scenic locations. Mandi, a popular destination for paragliding and other adventure activities, draws tourists from across the country. While such activities provide thrilling experiences, they necessitate stringent safety protocols and immediate response mechanisms for potential emergencies. The swift action by local residents and the administration in coordinating the power shutdown and organizing the rescue operation was crucial in averting a potential tragedy. The deployment of a crane, a vital piece of equipment for high-altitude rescues, proved instrumental in the success of the mission. The readiness of the Air Force helicopter as a backup underscores the gravity of the situation and the multi-agency coordination involved in managing such critical incidents in remote or challenging terrains. This event serves as a reminder of the importance of adhering to safety guidelines and the critical role of emergency services in ensuring the well-being of participants in adventure sports. The efficient response in Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, demonstrated the capability of local authorities and community members to collaborate effectively during crises, ensuring the safe recovery of the stranded pilot.

headline: Himachal Pradesh: Sudden Snowfall Strands Tourists, Vehicles at Kullu’s Jalori Jot
content: A sudden and unexpected snowfall at Jalori Jot, a high-altitude pass in Himachal Pradesh's Kullu district, disrupted traffic on Monday night, leaving numerous tourists and vehicles stranded. The extreme weather conditions necessitated immediate rescue operations by local authorities.Snowfall Disrupts Traffic, Strands TravellersThe pass, situated at an elevation of approximately 10,280 feet on the Aut-Luhri National Highway NH-305, experienced fresh snowfall. Accompanying the snow were freezing temperatures and icy road surfaces, rendering vehicle movement perilous. Near the Bada Nala stretch, about an inch of snow accumulated on the roadway, compelling officials to halt all vehicular traffic, including both small and large vehicles.Information was available with The Chenab Times indicating that the Kullu Superintendent of Police, Abishek Sekar, confirmed the disruption and the subsequent rescue efforts. Responding promptly to distress calls, the district police initiated a rescue operation to assist those stranded.Rescue Operation UnderwayA dedicated police rescue team was dispatched to the affected area. The team successfully evacuated approximately eight two-wheelers and 12 pedestrians and trekkers who found themselves stranded near Jalori Jot due to the sudden inclement weather. The rescued individuals were safely transported to Sojha in a government vehicle. Additionally, two small cars were towed across Jalori Top. Some drivers chose to return via the Gadagushaini route, opting for a safer journey back.In light of the escalating severity of the situation, local residents and taxi operators in the nearby tourist hubs of Sojha, Ghiyagi, and Jibhi were instructed by the SP to prevent tourists from proceeding towards Jalori Jot. They were also tasked with informing travellers about the current adverse road conditions and the risks associated with the journey.Advisory Issued to TouristsThe Superintendent of Police issued a strong appeal to all tourists, local residents, and vehicle drivers, urging them to refrain from travelling towards Jalori Jot, particularly during nighttime. He advised them to postpone their journeys until the weather conditions improve and the roads become safe for travel. The appeal also cautioned against the risks of driving on snow-covered and slippery roads, emphasizing the importance of adhering to directives from the police and administration.Further advice was given to travellers to meticulously plan their trips only after obtaining accurate information regarding weather forecasts and road conditions. The SP stressed the need to avoid unnecessary risks, particularly in treacherous mountain terrain during periods of snowfall and extreme cold.Intensified Cold in Rohtang Pass AreaMeanwhile, the cold wave has intensified significantly in the Rohtang Pass region. The area has witnessed fresh snowfall, accompanied by a sharp decline in temperatures. The drastic drop in temperature has led to the freezing of water in natural springs and small streams, creating a starkly cold landscape.Despite the harsh conditions, the natural ice formations at Rahni Nala have become a point of attraction for tourists. Visitors were observed capturing the scenic beauty of these natural ice formations through photographs, appreciating the unique spectacle presented by the frozen environment. The continued cold spell underscores the challenging winter conditions prevalent in the higher altitudes of Himachal Pradesh.

headline: Sacred Heart Senior Secondary School, Sector 26, Chandigarh, successfully concluded its two-day Annual Function 2026 with immense splendour and enthusiasm in the school auditorium on November 5 and 6.
content: CHANDIGARH, NOVEMBER 10, 2026 — Sacred Heart Senior Secondary School, Sector 26, Chandigarh, successfully concluded its two-day Annual Function 2026 with immense splendour and enthusiasm in the school auditorium on November 5 and 6. The grand spectacle, titled "The Awakening: A Sacred Symphony," held double significance this year, marking the 125th Anniversary (Quasquicentennial Jubilee) of the Clarist Franciscan Missionaries of the Most Blessed Sacrament (CFMSS) in India alongside the 800th Transitus Centenary of Saint Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of ecology. The opening day, featuring vibrant performances by students of Classes II and IV, was graced by Mr. Rakesh Arya, IPS (IG, Crime Branch, Haryana Police) as the Chief Guest, and Dr. Sulbha Arya as the Guest of Honour. On the second day, students of Classes III and V took the stage, with Mr. Nitish Singla, PCS (Director of School Education, Chandigarh Administration) honoring the occasion as Chief Guest alongside Guest of Honour Mr. Avneesh Tiwari, IRS (Additional Director, Directorate of Enforcement). Across both days, the young Sacred Heartians brought the five elements of nature—Sky, Air, Fire, Water, and Earth—to life on stage in graceful unison through expressive choreography, choral melodies, and dramatic acts that portrayed how human negligence and unchecked technology threaten environmental harmony. The overarching musical ballet served as a powerful reminder to cherish and preserve our planet, culminating in the inspiring teachings of Saint Francis of Assisi. The Chief Guests on both days commended the school management, teachers, and young artists for delivering a performance of artistic excellence paired with a deep social conscience. School Principal Rev. Sr. Venita Joseph warm-heartedly welcomed the dignitaries and expressed her profound gratitude to the management, faculty, students, and parents, highlighting that the production reflects Sacred Heart’s enduring legacy of value-based education, nurturing conscientious young citizens rooted in faith, compassion, and environmental care. headline: 20 years of service recognised: Retired woman IAF officer wins 15-year legal battle for pension as AFT alters ruling
content: The Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT), Chandigarh Bench at Chandimandir in Panchkula, has directed the Union government to treat retired Indian Air Force officer Wing Commander Namrita Chandi as having completed 20 years of pensionable service, making her eligible for pension and other retirement benefits. The tribunal ruled that Chandi, who served in the Indian Air Force (IAF) under the Short Service Commission (SSC), would be entitled to pensionary benefits applicable to an officer completing 20 years of qualifying service. According to a report in The Tribune, the bench modified its earlier 2015 judgment and directed that her pension should be granted with effect from the day following the completion of 20 years of service. IAF officer was initially granted 10-year Short Service Commission Wing Commander Chandi received her Short Service Commission in the Indian Air Force in 1996 for an initial tenure of 10 years. Before completing the tenure, she applied for Permanent Commission (PC). However, instead of granting her Permanent Commission, the Air Force authorities offered her a five-year extension. Her request was rejected on the grounds that the applicable rules did not provide for Permanent Commission to Short Service Commission officers in the flying branch. She subsequently retired from service in 2011. Chandi challenged the denial of Permanent Commission by filing a writ petition before the Delhi High Court in 2011. The matter was transferred to the Principal Bench of the Armed Forces Tribunal in 2014. In 2015, the tribunal allowed her petition along with several other cases, relying on the Delhi High Court's judgment in Babita Puniya and Others Vs. The Secretary and Another. The Union government challenged the decision before the Supreme Court, but its appeal was dismissed in 2019. Air Force sets up board to assess Permanent Commission eligibility Following a legal notice from Chandi, the Air Force authorities informed her that the competent authority had decided to examine her suitability for Permanent Commission. An independent board of officers was constituted, and she was asked to undergo a medical examination on July 22, 2020, if she was willing to accept the offer. However, Chandi objected to being assessed under the selection criteria prescribed in the 2004 and 2010 policies, particularly as she had been out of service for nearly nine years. Tribunal relies on SC judgments in women's commission cases Representing Chandi, advocate Sandeep Bansal argued that she was entitled to pension and other retirement benefits applicable to officers who had completed 20 years of pensionable service. He sought modification of the tribunal's 2015 order, relying on Supreme Court decisions concerning Permanent Commission for women officers in the Army and Navy, including Babita Puniya and Lt Cdr Annie Nagaraja and Others. The bench, comprising Justice Sudhir Mittal and Lieutenant General (Dr) Ranbir Singh (retd), rejected the Union government's request for an adjournment on the ground that the paper book was unavailable. It observed that the Supreme Court's relevant orders were already well known. The tribunal clarified that the benefit was intended for officers who had approached the Supreme Court and retired during the intervening period. Referring specifically to the Lt Cdr Annie Nagaraja judgment, the bench noted the Supreme Court's direction that women officers who had been denied consideration for Permanent Commission and were no longer in service should be deemed to have completed the requisite substantive pensionable service.Pension payable from completion of 20 years of serviceModifying its 2015 judgment, the AFT directed that Wing Commander Chandi be treated as having completed 20 years of pensionable service.It ordered that she be granted pension from the day immediately following the completion of 20 years of service, along with all other retiral benefits admissible to an officer completing the prescribed pensionable service.The ruling provides her relief after a prolonged legal battle over Permanent Commission and the pensionary benefits arising from her service in the Indian Air Force.

headline: Himachal-born Abhishek Awasthi becomes first Indian-origin Mayor of Australian city
content: CHANDIGARH: India-born Abhishek Awasthi, 43, who hails from Mandi in Himachal Pradesh, has been elected Mayor of the City of Greater Bendigo in Australia, becoming the first person of Indian origin to hold the post.He was unanimously elected for the 2026-2027 term at a special meeting of the Greater Bendigo City Council on Monday evening. The election was held at The Capital Theatre in Bendigo, with around 250 people attending the event. Councillor Andrea Metcalf was elected Deputy Mayor.Awasthi, who previously served as Deputy Mayor, will lead the council for a one-year term. He became Greater Bendigo's first Indian-origin Deputy Mayor for the 2024-2025 term, serving alongside then Mayor Andrea Metcalf.The City of Greater Bendigo is a local government area in Victoria, Australia.After being chosen for the position, Awasthi thanked his fellow councillors for their support and expressed gratitude to his parents, relatives and all those who had supported him throughout his journey. He also said he would work to meet the expectations of Greater Bendigo residents.“I am truly honoured and humbled to have been elected Mayor of the City of Greater Bendigo. Thank you to my fellow Councillors for their trust and confidence, and to our community for the opportunity to serve,” Awasthi wrote on Facebook.Awasthi hails from Lower Samkhetar in Mandi and went to Australia in 2008 to pursue higher education. He enrolled at La Trobe University, where he completed studies in biotechnology and later earned a master's degree in bioinformatics. Alongside his studies, he also took up part-time work. He became an Australian citizen in 2015 and lives in Greater Bendigo with his wife, Anima, and daughter, Agni.Over the years, Awasthi held several important positions in the Victorian state government. After settling in Bendigo in 2010, he began engaging with local community groups, taking up volunteering opportunities and participating in initiatives aimed at promoting multiculturalism.He entered local government after winning the councillor's election from the city's Kennington Ward in November 2024. Greater Bendigo has nine wards.He also founded the Indian Association of Bendigo, which was officially formed in 2021. The organisation works to connect Indian families across central Victoria through cultural events, charitable initiatives and community support programmes.Awasthi's parents, who were present at the swearing-in ceremony along with other relatives, shared in the occasion. His father, Surender Pal, is retired from the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), while his mother, Champa Sharma, is a homemaker..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Delhi govt announces public holiday on Chhath
content: 10/11/26 | 4:35 pm | Chhath Puja | Delhi govt announces public holiday on Chhath All government offices will remain closed as the Delhi government on Tuesday announced a public holiday on the occasion of Chhath Puja, according to an official order. “The Lieutenant Governor of the National Capital Territory of Delhi is pleased to declare 16 November, 2026 (Monday) to be a holiday in all government offices, autonomous bodies and Public Sector Undertakings, on account of Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi (Chhath Puja),” the order said. Earlier, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta had said Chhath is not merely a religious celebration but also a symbol of Delhi’s social and cultural unity. The government wants every devotee observing the fast and every visitor to celebrate the festival with complete faith, respect and peace of mind, she had said. Ahead of the four-day festival beginning on November 13, Gupta on Monday chaired a high-level review meeting and directed officials to give priority to devotees’ convenience, safety and cleanliness.

headline: Delhi to set up medical college at Guru Gobind Singh govt hospital with 150 MBBS, 40 PG seats
content: New Delhi: In a step towards strengthening medical education and public healthcare infrastructure, the Delhi Government is set to establish a medical college at Guru Gobind Singh Government Hospital (GGSGH), Raghubir Nagar, with 150 MBBS seats and 40 postgraduate seats.The proposed medical college will come up on the hospital's existing 13-acre campus and will be developed as per the guidelines of the National Medical Commission (NMC). The project is also part of a larger plan to expand healthcare facilities in the area by developing a 1,322-bed medical complex.The proposed complex will include an 850-bed General Hospital and a 472-bed Maternal and Child Hospital. The new General Hospital is being developed on around eight acres in Raghubir Nagar.Also read- Delhi plans to add 300 MBBS, 103 PG medical seatsThe expansion is expected to improve access to emergency care, specialised treatment and other medical facilities for nearly 10 lakh residents of West Delhi, who depend on government healthcare services in the region.Speaking about the development, Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh told ANI that the government is committed to strengthening medical education while ensuring affordable and quality healthcare for the people of Delhi. He further stated that, under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, the initiative reflects the government's commitment to expanding healthcare infrastructure and addressing the growing medical needs of the city's population. The Health Minister also highlighted that the proposed medical college, along with the expanded hospital facilities, would contribute towards building a stronger and more accessible healthcare system in the coming years. With the proposed expansion, West Delhi is poised to gain improved healthcare infrastructure, increased medical education opportunities and better access to essential and specialised medical services.A government official told HT, "The infrastructure will strengthen access to specialised medical services, emergency treatment and critical care for residents of the region."Meanwhile, Kumar said, "The Delhi government is committed to building a robust healthcare ecosystem that combines quality medical education with accessible and advanced treatment facilities. The establishment of this medical college, alongside the expansion of the associated hospitals, reflects our seriousness towards meeting people’s healthcare needs and creating long-term capacity for the future."Also read- Delhi proposes 108 MD, MS, DNB, Fellowship seats at 10 govt medical institutes
